decision_excerpt: Use scripts/pddr.py for init and validate, depend only on the Python standard library, reuse the same CLI in GitHub Actions, and stop before writing on conflicts.
context_dependency_reason: A mature YAML dependency is a reasonable generic engineering choice; the project-specific decision deliberately accepts a narrower metadata grammar to preserve zero-extra-dependency portability.

distractor_plausibility.A: Shell plus separate CI tooling is a common bootstrap pattern.
distractor_plausibility.B: A mature YAML library is a conventional extensibility choice.
distractor_plausibility.D: Cross-language tooling is plausible for teams already using Node and Python.

decision_excerpt: Treat PDDRs as Decision Context/Evidence rather than executable policy; current instructions and approved policy take precedence; select only the minimum relevant records.
context_dependency_reason: Completeness-first institutional-memory retrieval is a defensible generic RAG strategy, while this project explicitly prioritizes policy separation and minimum relevant context.

distractor_plausibility.B: Loading all accepted records minimizes omission risk.
distractor_plausibility.C: Recency filtering is a common heuristic when policy freshness matters.
distractor_plausibility.D: Compiling history into policy can simplify downstream consumption.

decision_excerpt: Track only Kit-managed files by hash, support dry-run, stop all writes on a managed-file mismatch, and never auto-update project-owned config, records, docs, rules, or CI.
context_dependency_reason: A three-way merge is a normal upgrade strategy for locally edited generated files; this project deliberately chose a fail-closed hash contract instead.

distractor_plausibility.A: Three-way merge preserves local edits while accepting upstream changes.
distractor_plausibility.B: Backup-and-replace is a simple package upgrade model.
distractor_plausibility.C: Treating a dedicated tool directory as package-owned is common.

decision_excerpt: Publish PDDR Kit as MIT OSS; keep common specification/templates/Skill/validation in the kit, project-specific records in each project, coexist with ADR/DDR, and keep paid semantic services optional.
context_dependency_reason: Both a central knowledge repository and project-local records are defensible organizational choices; the project-specific split must come from the decision history.

distractor_plausibility.A: A hosted service simplifies cross-project discovery.
distractor_plausibility.C: A central monorepo creates one searchable source of truth.
distractor_plausibility.D: Private incubation can reduce early compatibility commitments.

decision_excerpt: Keep init non-destructive; explicitly guide README discovery, AI/developer rules, CI connection, and Issue/PDDR boundaries; do not auto-edit project-specific files in v0.1.
context_dependency_reason: Auto-patching common README/CI patterns is a reasonable product-UX optimization, but the adoption evidence led this project to retain a manual project-specific integration boundary.

distractor_plausibility.C: A git hook can enforce usage without patching docs.
distractor_plausibility.D: Minimal installers often leave integration conventions to adopters.

decision_excerpt: Evaluate the skill with structured behavior cases covering routing, record action, state, required behaviors, and forbidden behaviors; real-model execution is required before claiming validated.
context_dependency_reason: A strong-model judge is a common modern evaluation approach; the project instead chose a portable explicit behavior contract because certain failures must be hard failures.

distractor_plausibility.A: LLM judges handle semantically equivalent wording well.
distractor_plausibility.B: Golden responses make regressions easy to diff.
distractor_plausibility.D: State-only scoring is deterministic and compact.

decision_excerpt: Add delivery_status=unknown; absence of implementation evidence must not be converted into not-started.
context_dependency_reason: Many project trackers use not-started as the default when no work is visible; this project explicitly rejected that inference and added unknown.

distractor_plausibility.A: not-started is a common default workflow state.
distractor_plausibility.B: Accepted decisions often imply planned implementation.
distractor_plausibility.C: not-applicable can be used when a dimension cannot be assessed.

decision_excerpt: Generated translations are review artifacts, not publication actions; keep repository writes out of the translation workflow and require human review before publication.
context_dependency_reason: Automatically opening/merging a CI-green translation PR is a plausible docs-automation policy; this project intentionally retained a separate human publication checkpoint.

distractor_plausibility.A: Direct CI writes minimize maintenance overhead.
distractor_plausibility.C: Generated PRs are a common automation boundary.
distractor_plausibility.D: Confidence gating is a plausible additional publication signal.

decision_excerpt: Translate complete protected lines; allow inline-token reordering; deterministically restore line-leading Markdown syntax; retry bounded line failures; keep unresolved structural corruption as a hard failure.
context_dependency_reason: AST-based translation is a reasonable generic structural-safety design, while this project chose a targeted whole-line patch to preserve natural grammar with bounded repair.

distractor_plausibility.B: Fragment translation fixes token positions deterministically.
distractor_plausibility.C: Prompt plus parser is simpler and preserves larger context.
distractor_plausibility.D: AST transformation is a conventional structured-document approach.

decision_excerpt: Mask protected terms and source==target glossary identities before translation; restore them afterward; send only source!=target entries to glossary enforcement; mask longer literals first.
context_dependency_reason: Boundary-aware post-processing is a plausible generic fix for substring collisions; the project instead separated identity masking from translation preferences after dogfooding.

distractor_plausibility.A: Boundary-aware replacement directly addresses substring collisions.
distractor_plausibility.B: Letting the model handle short identities reduces masking complexity.
distractor_plausibility.D: A final invariant check is a common validation-only design.

decision_excerpt: Use one reviewed OpenAI profile, exact POST endpoint, no redirects/relay, paced and capped requests, narrow key exposure, pinned translator dependencies, and do not describe the fetch guard as a complete sandbox.
context_dependency_reason: Container isolation with short-lived credentials is a plausible generic security architecture; this project froze a narrower request-guard profile and explicitly documented its remaining process trust.

distractor_plausibility.A: Container isolation is a standard third-party-code control.
distractor_plausibility.B: A relay can centralize retries and egress policy.
distractor_plausibility.C: Configurable endpoints improve reuse while spend limits cap cost.

decision_excerpt: Caller owns canonical content, languages, terminology, provider secret/budget, repository-specific semantic checks, review and publication; kit owns generic mechanics; reviewed production use pins an immutable SHA or release tag.
context_dependency_reason: Following main while keeping caller policy local is a plausible continuous-delivery design; this project chose explicit immutable pins to make upgrades reviewed and reproducible.

distractor_plausibility.D: Central policy plus immutable pins maximizes consistency.
